title: Floating bodies find rest in orbit
description: Sleeping in microgravity requires more than just closing your eyes. Discover how astronauts anchor themselves to drift into dreams while orbiting our planet.
instagram_caption: Even in the silent void of space, rest is a necessity. Follow Wonders of the Nature for more stories like this.

segments.narration: This dark cabin appears quiet, but drifting bodies risk colliding with sharp instruments.
broll_queries: astronaut sleeping in space close up
international space station interior wide shot

segments.narration: To stay still, the weary traveler needs to anchor against the drifting walls.
Without gravity, the body naturally curls into a relaxed, fetal position every time.
They zip themselves inside a padded bag to prevent limbs from floating away.
broll_queries: astronaut zipping sleeping bag close up
sleeping quarters inside station wide shot

segments.narration: Small straps secure this cocoon to the wall, keeping the dreamer perfectly still.
broll_queries: straps on sleeping bag close up

segments.narration: Air vents hum constantly to circulate oxygen while preventing dangerous carbon dioxide pockets.
If air flow stops, an astronaut might wake up struggling to breathe deep.
Headphones muffle the constant drone of pumps and cooling systems behind the walls.
The morning sun rises rapidly, signaling a new day in the silent void.
